reason: Our terms already put agent risk on the customer, and my engineers already rate-limit every API key, so I don't have a problem that's costing me money today. I'm not putting an unaudited startup's proxy in the trade path before Robinhood or Coinbase show me this is the standard.
objection: A company with no customers and no SOC 2 sitting inline in front of every agent order. If it goes down or gets it wrong, that's my outage and my regulator conversation, and they can't absorb any of that.
would_change_my_mind: Robinhood or Coinbase rolling out agent passport checks or a gate like this, or FINRA saying it expects firms to have controls on customer agents beyond terms of service.
